Subject: Tenant-level TTL + region selection for customer data

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. One follow-up from our security and legal teams: we need the ability to set TTL/deletion policies at the tenant (customer) level and to pin storage of the retained artifacts (logs, embeddings, KV cache snapshots) to EU-only regions. Key asks:

- Tenant-scoped TTLs (per-environment/tenant) with overrides for shorter retention.
- Option to force storage to an EU region (no cross-region backups).
- API hooks or webhooks for deletion events so our audit system can reconcile deletes immediately.
- Exportable audit log entries for deletions (for SOC2 evidence).

Can you share whether this is on your roadmap, expected ETA, and whether there are any constraints (e.g., migration work for existing tenants)? Procurement also asked whether this impacts pricing or Dedicated/Private options.

Appreciate a short write-up we can share internally.

Thanks,
Anna

Anna / team — thanks for sending this. Below is a concise product summary we can share internally and with FinGuard. High level: we plan a phased approach that gives Hosted customers tenant-level retention controls and explicit region selection flags; Dedicated/Private customers will get additional contractual/ops guardrails.

Product summary (draft):
- Tenant TTL controls: per-tenant (and per-route) TTL config with minimum/maximum bounds and an API to update. Default inherited from org-level policy.
- Region pinning: a "region_selection" flag on tenant config that constrains storage regions (EU / US / APAC). For Hosted, this will route data only to compatible regions and avoid cross-region backups.
- Deletion hooks: asynchronous webhook when TTL-triggered deletion completes + exportable deletion audit lines (timestamp, deleted object id, triggering policy, operator-id).
- Migration: existing data will need backfilled flags; for tenants requesting immediate EU-only residency we will offer a one-time migration plan with estimated downtime/throughput impact.

Open product/engineering questions:
1) Does FinGuard require immediate hard-delete (irreversible) vs soft-delete + retention window?
2) What SLA for deletion/audit export do they expect (real-time, hourly batch)?
3) Any existing encryption/KMS constraints (customer-managed keys)?

I'll draft a short doc for FinGuard. Karthik — can you comment on feasibility and rough ETA for Hosted baseline (tenant TTL + region flag) vs Dedicated/Private hardened controls?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Team / Anna — technical summary and rough estimates below. High-level feasibility: straightforward for control-plane + metadata; storage routing and migration are the heavier pieces.

Technical notes:
- Tenant TTL: implement as metadata on tenant + scheduled background sweeper that removes objects based on TTL. For embeddings and logs we can leverage existing blob lifecycle hooks. Estimated effort: 4–6 engineer-weeks to deliver a basic hosted API (CRUD for TTL, enforcer, and sweeper).
- Region pinning (Hosted): requires runtime routing to region-local storage endpoints and disabling cross-region replication. If we treat this as a per-tenant placement policy in our scheduler, effort is ~6–8 engineer-weeks (routing + testing + compliance checks).
- Deletion webhooks & audit exports: lightweight additional API & queue work — ~2–3 engineer-weeks. Export formats for SOC2 can be implemented as CSV/JSON with signatures.
- Migration for existing tenants to EU-only: non-trivial. We'll need a controlled migration job that copies data to EU bucket, validates checksums, and then deletes non-EU copies. Estimated runbook + infra work: 3–4 engineer-weeks and potential IO cost; migrations for large tenants may incur temporary throughput degradation.

Constraints & notes:
- Hosted vs Dedicated: Dedicated/Private gets easier compliance (no shared control plane), but Hosted can meet policy if region pinning is enforced and cross-region backups are disabled per-tenant.
- KMS: if a customer requires CMK (customer-managed keys) scoped to region, that adds extra work (integration with KMS partners) — tack on 2–4 weeks depending on provider.
- Audit latency: "real-time" deletion notifications are possible via streaming, but will increase operational complexity compared to hourly batch exports.

Rough timeline options (start-to-shippable):
- Minimal: TTL + deletion webhooks (hosted) — 6–8 weeks (one sprint + stabilization).
- Full: TTL + region pinning + deletion webhooks + audit exports — 10–14 weeks.
- Migration runbook & tooling for large tenants — add 3–4 weeks parallel to Full.

I'll also open an RFC and spike ticket for region-aware scheduler changes and migration tooling.

Karthik
